# SpeakX · Sia’s October 2026 production calendar

Planning pack, not rendered or published content. All 31 dates use Asia/Kolkata (IST). October 1 is Thursday; October 31 is Saturday. Supplied prompts are reference material; this calendar covers the requested full month, uses Sia alone and includes virtual location lessons. No platform account or media provider has been connected by this content plan.

## What ships

- 31 original teaching episodes: 19 A1/A2 (61.3%), 9 B1 (29.0%), 3 B2 (9.7%).
- 62 primary video placements: one Instagram Reel and one Facebook video/Reel daily.
- 62 X text placements: a morning tip at 08:30 and an evening exercise at 19:00 daily. X video is an optional replacement for an evening post, not an extra assumed placement.
- 31 Instagram Story sets at 09:00 daily, three frames each (93 frames). Repurpose to Facebook Stories only after account capability and review are confirmed; these are excluded from the base count.
- Base: 155 scheduled units (62 video posts + 62 X posts + 31 Story sets), representing 217 individual posts/frames. There are 31 lessons, not 155 unique lessons.
- 31 word selections are unique within this month. Check the historical word bank before production to enforce the 90-day no-repeat policy; history was not supplied.

## Production rules

Each episode targets a final 35–45-second video. Revised scripts contain 43–69 spoken words, excluding bracketed silent directions. Timing estimates use a careful 1.8 words/second, a two-second practice pause (plus three one-second answer pauses on Sundays), and two seconds for transitions. All estimates are below 45 seconds. Short scripts leave time for slower target pronunciation and quiet reading/answer holds; the renderer must measure actual duration. Never speed up the target English to force a fit. Bracketed text is silent and not sent to TTS. On Mondays the full word lesson replaces the closing word segment.

Render a 1920×1080 landscape master and a 1080×1920 vertical reframing. Instagram gets vertical; Facebook gets its approved vertical or landscape version. X’s base plan is text; optional video uses the approved ≤45-second cut. Supply SRT/caption tracks, a cover, transcript, alt text, music licence reference and render QA report with every video. Keep lower 20% and right 12% of vertical layouts clear of essential text and faces. Use the exact supplied SpeakX logo on end cards.

Only Sia appears and speaks. No interviewer, café staff, classroom children, background crowds, reflections or second synthetic voice. Dialogue partners appear as clearly labelled question cards; Sia speaks only her response. Sia remains visually locked to the supplied character board: face, hair, grey outfit, warm style. The default is the pale-blue studio. Location codes map to the confirmed categories: FND = food/café, EDU = education, OFC = office/interview, AIR = airport. STU is the default studio, not a physical map category. Every record currently carries `mapPinStatus: Awaiting map`. Managers must upload location maps, select a category and choose a pin before claiming a real location. Named virtual sets below are proposed teaching contexts; no real SpeakX locations or addresses were supplied. Use language such as “Aaj interview room mein practice karte hain,” never imply Sia visited a real branch. Once the team provides cleared location photos/addresses, replace the set with the approved place and re-review. The current request allows location variation despite the older reference’s fixed-background rule.

The character board is not an audio source. Sia_v1 is a planned voice identifier pending source audio, documented rights/consent where applicable and voice approval. Do not substitute a random voice. Audio direction: warm Hinglish, neutral Indian English, slower target English, two-second practice pause; gentle licensed/original music under speech and one answer chime. No music or sound may cover pronunciation.

Captions and scripts are drafts requiring human language and media review. Incorrect examples must carry a visible WRONG/❌ label while shown; do not expose an incorrect phrase alone on a cover. No user-count, ranking, guarantee, price or outcome claims. The pronunciation guides are production aids, not phonetic transcriptions.

## Scheduling and operations

Weekdays: Instagram 19:30; Facebook 20:00. Weekends: Instagram 11:00; Facebook 11:30. X: daily 08:30 and 19:00. Stories: daily 09:00. These are starting hypotheses, not proven best times. Compare time-slot performance within the same platform, format, topic and metric age; do not infer success from one post. Store UTC in production, show IST to managers.

First batch (Oct 1–4): script lock Sep 24, media QA Sep 28, approval Sep 29. Oct 5–11: production ready Oct 1, approval Oct 2. Oct 12–18: ready Oct 8, approval Oct 9. Oct 19–25: ready Oct 15, approval Oct 16. Oct 26–31: ready Oct 22, approval Oct 23. Each “ready” batch includes all videos, captions, stories and X text. Missing approval at a slot means skip and review a new time, never automatic release.

Weekly reports: Oct 5, 12, 19, 26 and Nov 2 at 13:00 IST. A report uses only available snapshots and flags immature posts. October month-end report on Nov 2 is preliminary; complete the final +30-day cohort report after Nov 30. Do not silently replace already approved posts based on analytics; proposed changes return to review.

### 2026-10-06 · Grammar Tuesday

**Am, is and are · A1 · 35–45-second video**

Set: Pale-blue studio · STU · Awaiting map. Target: I am ready. He is ready. We are ready.

Word: **Calm** — shaant; relaxed and not worried. Example: Stay calm.

Hook option B: Sia ke saath bolo: I am ready. He is ready. We are ready.

**Complete spoken draft**

He am ready? Ek chhota fix! Hi, main Sia! I ke saath am. He, she, it ke saath is. You, we, they ke saath are. I am ready. He is ready. We are ready. [❌ WRONG: He am ready.] Bolke dekho: We are ready. [2-second pause] Aaj ka word: Calm. shaant. Stay calm. Apna sentence comment karo. Kal milte hain!
